transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Ortega, Priya Rao (Redwood); Anika Patel, Marcus Liu, Sophie Grant, Devon Reyes (Timberline)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): QBR-style renewal check; customer wants EU region and a small dedicated pool; procurement timeline in two weeks; SE to run perf tests; security notes about PII and KMS.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for making time. We're here to go over the renewal and the expansion items you flagged — EU region and the modest dedicated bump. Quick intros?
[00:09] Anika (VP of ML): Hi, Anika here. We're looking to go live in EU for latency reasons and also to satisfy some residency asks. Marcus on infra, Sophie from procurement.
[00:18] Marcus (Infra): Hey, yeah, Marcus. Main ask is predictable latency under 120ms p90 for inference. We want to understand routing and fallback policies.
[00:25] Liam (SE): Cool, quick note — the EU activation path has two options: hosted EU nodes on our infra or VPC private deployment. Each has different lead times and SLA.
[00:35] Sophie (Procurement): And from our side, procurement needs firm dates for activation before we sign the amendment. We also need an updated SOW to include the new region and committed capacity.
[00:44] Maya: Understood. Our proposal is a 20% committed capacity bump (small cluster of dedicated GPUs) and EU hosted region with optional VPC path later. That keeps time-to-activation faster.
[00:55] Devon (SRE): Quick question, if you go hosted EU, where is the KV cache stored? Will there be cross-region latency for cold starts?
[01:03] Liam: Good, yes. For hosted EU we keep the KV cache local to the EU cluster. Cold starts for long sessions could still hit a warm-up cost; our continuous batching and prefix caching help mitigate that. There's also an automatic fallback to a cross-region variant if local capacity is saturated but that would add latency.
[01:22] Anika: We ran a small internal spike against a US region and saw p95 at ~190ms for our chat flows, with lots of long context. We need p90 <120ms in EU. Can you run an apples-to-apples perf test?
[01:33] Liam: Absolutely. We'll spin up an EU instance and run the same prompt set. Can you send the prompt corpus and a sample of sequence lengths?
[01:40] Anika: Yep, I'll share. There may be some redacted PII in samples — we'll redact but want confirmation on how Redwood handles that data in logs.
[01:48] Priya (CSM): On the data handling side, we keep audit logs and offer KMS integrations for keys. We can show the security datasheet and SOC2 excerpts.
[01:56] Sophie: Also, can you confirm retention windows and whether logs used for quality monitoring are kept in plaintext? Procurement needs that for the DPA.
[02:05] Maya: We have a standard DPA, logs retention defaults to 30 days but configurable. We can push the security doc and DPA redline notes after this call.
[02:13] Marcus: Regarding routing and fallbacks — what happens if the EU cluster is saturated? Is there automatic routing to a cheaper region and what about model variant changes?
[02:22] Liam: Policy-driven routing: we can route by latency, cost, or strictly by region. Fallbacks can route to a compatible smaller quantized variant or to US region. We'll share our recommendation: EU-first, then fallback to a pinned quantized variant in the same region if possible, else failover to US with an explicit flag so you can monitor quality impact.
[02:41] Anika: Okay. From ML perspective, the quality cost of quantization is a concern; we need an eval on our prompt set when you run benchmarks so we can see quality before agreeing.
[02:50] Liam: Yeah we'll run both latency and regression tests — include prompt set, we will produce token-level cost, latency percentiles, and basic quality metrics (BLEU-ish for structured outputs, and a human-annotated quality sample).
[03:03] Maya: On pricing: the amendment will reflect per-region activation fees plus per-token for hosted EU; dedicated bump priced as monthly reserved capacity. We'll include a scenario with burst allowances.
[03:15] Sophie: For the contract—we need to know if the reserved capacity is refundable or flexible if usage doesn't ramp. Also, any termination windows?
[03:22] Maya: Standard reserved contracts have a 12-month minimum, with pro-rated refunds only in specific cases; we can propose a 90-day escalation clause or a pilot period to reduce risk. I'll put that in the draft.
[03:32] Devon: One more ops question: how do rollouts work? We want canary and A/B capability across regions during rollout.
[03:39] Liam: Rollouts are first-class — canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback. You can pin model versions per-route so you can gradually shift traffic between US and EU.
[03:47] Anika: Great. Timeline — we want EU live by mid-April. Procurement timeline aims to close by end of March. Is that feasible?
[03:56] Maya: Tight but doable. If we get the PO and sign-off by March 20, we can have hosted EU activation in 3-4 weeks plus perf validation. Dedicated VPC would take longer — typically 6-8 weeks.
[04:08] Sophie: March 20 PO is our internal goal. We'll try to get redlines before then.
[04:12] Maya: Perfect. I'll send an amendment, detailed pricing, and the security pack. Liam will schedule the EU perf run. Priya will pull usage/cost scenarios.
[04:21] Anika: One minor note — we're evaluating CloudAICo for price, they offered a faster trial but we saw variance in long-context throughput. We'll want Redwood's best latency numbers in writing.
[04:33] Maya: Understood — we'll include benchmark numbers and the test plan.
[04:37] Liam: For the perf test plan: we'll run 3 load profiles, low/medium/high, measure p50/p90/p95, token-cost, and run quality checks. We'll share raw traces and a summary sheet.
[04:50] Marcus: When you share raw traces, please strip any customer PII and mark where synthetic IDs were used.
[04:55] Priya: Noted. We'll also pull your last 90 days of token consumption and show cost deltas for the committed bump versus on-demand.
[05:04] Maya: Great. Any other outstanding items?
[05:07] Devon: One ask — can we get a short runbook describing how failover and throttling events are surfaced in the console and via webhooks?
[05:15] Maya: Yes, we'll include the runbook excerpt with alerting hooks and sample webhook payloads.
[05:20] Sophie: Okay that should be sufficient for procurement to move. We'll aim for internal sign-off by March 18 and final PO by March 20.
[05:28] Maya: Thanks everyone. Quick recap: Redwood to send amendment + pricing + security pack (Maya), SE to run EU perf tests (Liam), CSM to provide cost scenarios (Priya), Timberline to provide prompt corpus and PO timeline (Anika/Sophie).
[05:40] Anika: Thanks, talk soon.
[05:42] Meeting end.
